fee_exemptions: Vehicles re-entering solely to retrieve a shuttled car after finishing a backpacking trip -- confirmed verbally, in person, by EBRPD gate/entrance staff; not found in a published fee schedule.
gate_hours_conditions: May through Labor Day, 6am-9pm. THE CLOSING TIME IS DISPUTED AND 9PM IS KEPT AS THE STORED ANSWER -- see the del-valle-gate-close thread. ReserveAmerica's Del Valle page says 'Park entrance and campground gates close daily at 10 pm', and EBRPD's own District-wide booking alert says campground gates close at 10pm daily; the park page read on 2026-09-04 says 9pm. Two surfaces say ten and one says nine, and the nine is the oldest -- but this is kept because the costly direction is arriving at 9:30 on the strength of a ten and finding it shut, the same call made on Anthony Chabot's season. GROUP CAMPSITE GATE HOURS CHANGE SEASONALLY, per ReserveAmerica, and no seasonal band is published anywhere read. This project holds no group campsite at Del Valle at all, which is a gap in the campground list rather than in this row.
notes: Entrance fee/hours are from the official EBRPD page; the fee-exemption rule is a verbal, in-person staff confirmation, not yet independently found in writing -- treat with correspondingly lower confidence than the fee/hours figures. 7000 Del Valle Rd., Livermore, CA. Park phone 510-544-3139, distinct from the reservations line. FROM I-580 in Livermore, exit North Livermore Ave and head south through town -- it becomes South Livermore Ave, then Tesla Rd. About 1.5 miles past town turn right onto Mines Rd, go 3.5 miles, then continue straight onto Del Valle Rd where Mines Rd turns left; the entrance is about four miles on. That is roughly nine miles of back road after the freeway, which is worth knowing against a gate that shuts at nine or ten.

fee_conditions: Parking is free at Anthony Chabot, which is NOT the District-wide pattern -- Del Valle charges $10 on weekends and holidays, and Lake Chabot, reached from the same brochure and connected by trail, charges $5/vehicle. Free here is a fact about this park, not about EBRPD.
gate_hours_conditions: Campground and group camps. General park hours are 5am-10pm, so the campground gate opens three hours after the park does. Seasonal closures may affect park hours.
notes: 9999 Redwood Road, Castro Valley, CA 94546. Park office (510) 690-6676, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4502 -- distinct from the reservations line. Accepts cash, Visa, MasterCard and Discover. RV sewage disposal $20/use for non-campers. No day-use parking in the campground. Main entrance is Marciel Gate on Marciel Road, off Redwood Road.

fee_conditions: Charged only WHEN THE KIOSK IS ATTENDED -- seasonal, weekends and some holidays -- so the fee is neither always charged nor reliably avoidable. $5 per trailered vehicle; buses $25. Cash, Visa, MasterCard and Discover.

gate_hours_conditions: SEVEN SEASONAL BANDS, and this schema holds one closing time, so the bands are stated here rather than flattened into a single figure that would be wrong most of the year. Jan 1-Jan 30 8am-5pm; Jan 31-Mar 7 8am-6pm; Mar 8-Apr 3 8am-7pm; Apr 4-Sept 7 8am-8pm; Sept 8-Oct 9 8am-7pm; Oct 10-Oct 31 8am-6pm; Nov 1-Dec 31 8am-5pm. Opening is 8am in every band. A backpacker walking out from Stewartville, 3.2 miles in, has to clear the gate before it closes.
notes: 5175 Somersville Road, Antioch, CA 94509. Park office (510) 544-2750, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4506. No public WiFi. Greathouse Visitor Center is wheelchair accessible, with ADA restrooms and an accessible water fountain in the upper parking lot; accommodation requests need a week's notice on (510) 544-2750.

fee_conditions: Charged when the kiosk is attended. $5 per trailered vehicle; buses $25. BRIONES ONLY ACCEPTS CASH -- no cards of any kind, which is not the District pattern: Anthony Chabot and Black Diamond both take Visa, MasterCard and Discover. Arriving with a card and no notes means not paying, at a kiosk that may or may not be staffed.
gate_close: varies by season, 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM -- see conditions
gate_hours_conditions: SIX SEASONAL BANDS, stated rather than flattened because one closing time would be wrong most of the year: Jan 1-31 8am-5pm; Feb 1-Mar 13 8am-6pm; Mar 14-Apr 10 8am-7pm; Apr 11-Sept 5 8am-8pm; Sept 6-Nov 6 8am-7pm; Nov 7-Dec 31 8am-5pm. Opening is 8am in every band. TWO LIMITS, NOT ONE: PARKING LOT HOURS ARE 8am TO SUNSET, which is a different constraint from the gate and binds first whenever sunset falls before the gate closes. THE BANDS ARE PUBLISHED FOR ALHAMBRA AND BEAR CREEK ONLY -- the park's other three staging areas, Briones Road, Reliez Valley and Lafayette Ridge, have no hours stated on this page, and whether they follow the same schedule is UNCONFIRMED.
notes: 6,255 acres in Contra Costa County. Park office (510) 544-3121, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4508. FIVE STAGING AREAS, and two of them are a trap for each other: Briones Road Staging Area is at 2537 Reliez Valley Road, Martinez, while Reliez Valley Staging Area is at 1956 Reliez Valley Road, Lafayette -- different entrances, same road, names that point at each other. The others are Alhambra Staging Area at 273-181 Brookwood Dr, Martinez (called Alhambra Creek Staging Area elsewhere on the same page), Bear Creek Staging Area at 1611 Bear Creek Road, Lafayette, and Lafayette Ridge Staging Area, for which NO ADDRESS IS PUBLISHED. THREE GROUP CAMPSITES EXIST HERE, capacity 50 to 300, all with picnic tables, BBQ, fire ring and chemical toilets -- but this page names NONE of them, so no campground rows were created; naming them needs the booking system. The page states a minimum of 17 people for a group campsite, which is the District floor and NOT the per-site figure: the 2026 group camping table scales the minimum to 50 for a 100-capacity site and 100 for a 300-capacity one, and Briones' sites reach 300. THE BRIONES SPECIAL MANAGEMENT AREA is a 1,600-acre zone in the north-east of the park restricting trail use by mode and direction -- hiking only, biking only, or hiking and biking -- and ON WEEKENDS ALTERNATING BETWEEN BICYCLE AND EQUESTRIAN USE BY EVEN AND ODD CALENDAR DAYS. This project has no category for trail-use restrictions, so it is recorded here rather than as a rule. GRAZING CATTLE are in named trail areas: cows and calves in Tabletop, Spengler, Blue Oak, Buckeye, Sunrise and Lafayette Ridge; yearlings in Deer Creek, Pereirra, Valley and Briones Crest. That matters for dogs -- Ordinance 38 s.801.21 requires any animal to be leashed and under complete control where grazing animals are present.

gate_hours_conditions: SIX SEASONAL BANDS, the third park in this project to need more than one closing time: January 8am-5pm; Feb 1-Mar 12 8am-6pm; Mar 13-Apr 17 8am-7pm; Apr 18-Sept 5 8am-8pm; Sept 6-Nov 5 8am-7pm; Nov 6-Dec 31 8am-5pm. notes: 19450 Marsh Creek Road, Brentwood, CA. 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4556. 2,191 acres. No public WiFi. Drinking water, restrooms and a drinking fountain at the staging area, the restrooms and fountain being wheelchair accessible. NO DOGS ANYWHERE IN THE PARK. Temperatures commonly exceed 100F in summer.

gate_hours_conditions: SIX SEASONAL BANDS, AND THE FIRST PARK HERE WHERE THE OPENING TIME ALSO MOVES. Black Diamond, Briones and Round Valley all open at 8am in every band, so that one figure was storable; Coyote Hills opens at 7am for five months and 8am for seven. Jan-Feb 7am-6pm; Mar 7am-7pm; Apr-Sept 8am-8pm; Oct 8am-7pm; Nov 1-27 8am-6pm; Nov 28-Dec 31 7am-6pm. A SEPARATE PARK CURFEW RUNS 10pm-5am, which is not the same thing as the gate: the gate governs vehicle entry, the curfew governs being in the park at all, and between gate close and 10pm you may be present without being able to drive in or out.
notes: 8000 Patterson Ranch Road, Fremont, CA 94555. (510) 544-3220, or 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4519. 1,266 acres of marshland and grassland on the eastern shore of San Francisco Bay. Three entrances: the main entrance, Quarry Staging Area and Patterson Ranch Staging Area; nearest BART is Union City. Visitor Center 10am-4pm Wednesday to Sunday. Two disabled parking spaces at the Visitor Center, accessible stalls in both public restrooms, ADA-upgraded drinking fountains, and wheelchair-accessible chemical toilets in the Visitor Center lot and at Quarry Staging. Picnic cooking fires are limited to the metal braziers provided. The waters west and south are the Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge, run by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service -- a different agency, whose land this project does not hold, and DOGS ARE NOT ALLOWED IN THE REFUGE even though Coyote Hills itself permits them. ACREAGE IS REPORTED TWO WAYS AND NO CONFLICT THREAD IS OPENED FOR IT: the park page says 1,266 acres, ReserveAmerica's listing for the same park says 978. Neither figure changes a camping plan, and the same decision was taken for the drive times that disagreed earlier -- a conflict thread is for facts that change what someone does. Recorded so that a later reader meeting 978 somewhere does not think it is a correction. COORDINATES, from ReserveAmerica: 37.5575, -122.08583. The first coordinates stored anywhere in this project, and they are in prose because no table here has a field for them -- park_access, campgrounds and campsites all lack one. ONE MORE THING FROM THAT LISTING, filed as evidence rather than as fact: it says 'Dumbarton Quarry and Ardenwood Historic Farm parks are located nearby', calling Dumbarton a PARK located NEARBY on the same day this project resolved Dumbarton Quarry Campground's park field to Coyote Hills. See the campground's own row and the ebrpd-camping-park-count thread; the resolution stands on the brochure listing it under Coyote Hills' Camping heading, but it is no longer unopposed.

fee_conditions: Charged only WHEN THE KIOSK IS ATTENDED, so whether you pay depends on staffing rather than on the date -- the same wording Black Diamond and Briones carry, and no page here says what happens when it is unattended. $5 per trailered vehicle; buses $25. GARIN ONLY ACCEPTS CASH. That is the second cash-only park in this project after Briones, against Coyote Hills one park over taking Visa, MasterCard, Discover and tap to pay -- so payment method is a per-park fact in this District and cannot be carried from one park to the next.
gate_close: varies by season, 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM -- see conditions
gate_hours_conditions: SIX SEASONAL BANDS, AND THEY DO NOT COVER THE WHOLE YEAR. Nov 1-Mar 5 8am-6pm; Mar 6-Apr 16 8am-7pm; Apr 17-May 21 8am-8pm; May 22-Aug 27 8am-9pm; Aug 28-Sep 24 8am-8pm; Sep 25-Oct 29 8am-7pm. OCTOBER 30 AND 31 FALL IN NO BAND -- the last band ends Oct 29 and the next starts Nov 1. Two days a year have no published closing time at a park whose group camp tells you to 'check Garin gate hours and enter before closing time', and a party arriving on Halloween has nothing to check. Read as a gap in the source, not as a park that shuts: either band could be the intended one, and they differ by an hour. Opening is 8am in every band, so that figure is storable, unlike Coyote Hills. THE LATEST CLOSING TIME IN THIS PROJECT is Garin's 9pm summer band; every other park here shuts by 8pm. A SEPARATE PARK CURFEW RUNS 10pm-5am, distinct from the gate: the gate governs vehicle entry, the curfew governs being in the park at all.
notes: Garin: 1580 Garin Avenue, Hayward, CA 94544. Toll free 888-327-2757 option 3 extension 4530. THE ARROYO FLATS GROUP CAMP HAS A DIFFERENT STREET NUMBER ON THE SAME ROAD -- 1320 Garin Avenue, which is also the park's mailing address on ReserveAmerica, against the park page's 1580. Both are published by EBRPD. A party navigating to the wrong number is on the right road, so this is recorded rather than resolved. GARIN AND DRY CREEK PIONEER ARE TWO ADJOINING PARKS, described by EBRPD as 'two adjoining parks from former 19th Century ranches' and by ReserveAmerica as sharing 'a contiguous border with sister park Dry Creek Pioneer Regional Park'. Combined they are over 5,800 acres with more than 35 miles of trails. The camping is at Garin; nothing read gives Dry Creek Pioneer a camp of its own. See the ebrpd-camping-park-count thread -- this was the third candidate explanation for that gap and it is now evidenced. ACCESSIBILITY: wheelchair-accessible restrooms in the building by the Garin Barn, an accessible chemical toilet near Jordan Pond, accessible drinking fountains through the picnic area, and service roads around the meadows and picnic areas that are wheelchair accessible for between 0.25 and 0.5 miles. Disabled parking at the Garin lot at the end of Garin Avenue in Hayward and at the Dry Creek Garden lot at the end of May Road in Union City -- note that the second is in a different city, which is what an adjoining park looks like on the ground. The Garin Red Barn Visitor Center opens Sundays 10am-4pm, June 14 to September 6. Dry Creek Garden opens Thursday to Saturday 10am-4pm, but is CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE for storm damage -- see advisories. CATTLE ARE GRAZED HERE: EBRPD asks that dogs be heeled or leashed past cattle, warning that chasing may injure or kill them. No cell service or WiFi is stated for the camping area. FROM THE SHARED GARIN/DRY CREEK PIONEER MAP: one brochure covers both parks. Arroyo Flats is the only Reservable Camp symbol on it. FOUR RESERVABLE GROUP PICNIC AREAS sit at the Garin Avenue staging area -- Cattlemen's, Buttonwood and Ranchside at 100 people each and Pioneer at 50 -- with picnic tables and barbecue braziers. They are NOT campgrounds and are not in campgrounds.csv, the same call made for Briones' Oak Grove, Newt Hollow and Crow. THE PICNIC LEAD TIME CONTRADICTS ITSELF IN TWO PARAGRAPHS OF ONE PAGE: 'Reservations Department takes picnic reservations up to 3 working days prior to the event -- so the last day to reserve for the weekend would be Wednesday', then 'may be reserved by phoning EBRPD Reservations ... at least 14 days in advance of the planned event'. Three days or fourteen, on one page, about the same four areas. Nothing here books a picnic area, so no conflict thread is opened -- but it is the third EBRPD lead-time disagreement this project has found, after Briones' five-business-days brochure and Coyote Hills' five working days, and it is the first where a single page disagrees with itself. Whatever number an EBRPD page gives for a deadline, phone and confirm it. Also on the map: the Chabot-to-Garin Trail connects this parkland to Anthony Chabot, Jordan Pond sits near the Union City BART side by Kite Field, and a second staging area for Dry Creek Pioneer opens off Pulaski Drive.

fee_conditions: Charged only when the kiosk is attended. $5 per trailered vehicle; buses $25. ONE ASYMMETRY WORTH RECORDING AND NOT OVER-READING: Garin's page states 'Garin only accepts cash for payment' and this page, which is otherwise near-identical, says nothing about payment method at all. An absent sentence is not a statement that cards are taken. Bring cash.
gate_close: varies by season, 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM -- see conditions
gate_hours_conditions: IDENTICAL TO GARIN'S, BAND FOR BAND, INCLUDING THE GAP. Nov 1-Mar 5 8am-6pm; Mar 6-Apr 16 8am-7pm; Apr 17-May 21 8am-8pm; May 22-Aug 27 8am-9pm; Aug 28-Sep 24 8am-8pm; Sep 25-Oct 29 8am-7pm. OCTOBER 30 AND 31 FALL IN NO BAND here too, so the two-day hole is not a typo on one page -- EBRPD publishes the same incomplete schedule for both halves of this parkland. Park curfew 10pm-5am, as at Garin. The Dry Creek Garden parking lot is stated as open all week until dusk, which is a third time band and is not the same as either the gate or the curfew.
notes: Dry Creek Pioneer: 550 May Road, Union City, CA 94587. Same toll-free number and extension as Garin, 888-327-2757 option 3 ext. 4530 -- one phone line for two parks. THIS PARK HAS NO CAMPGROUND AND IS TAGGED FOR CAMPING. Its park page carries the Camping activity icon, there is no ReserveAmerica facility for it, and the single map covering both parks shows exactly one Reservable Camp symbol: Arroyo Flats, in the Garin half, keyed to the Garin Avenue Staging Area inset. See the ebrpd-camping-park-count thread -- this is the park that makes two of that conflict's three candidate explanations turn out to be the same park. HISTORY, from the park page: the Meyers sisters' 1,626-acre Dry Creek Ranch was donated to the District in 1979 and opened as Dry Creek Regional Park; the Meyers Cottage and its garden came later, on the death of the last surviving sister. The District plans eventually to open the cottage for receptions and a small visitor centre. ACCESS is the Dry Creek Staging Area at the end of May Road off Mission Blvd -- from I-880 exit Whipple Road east and continue straight onto May Road at Mission Blvd; from I-580 it is Mission Blvd for 5.9 miles then left on May Road. The map also names a DRY CREEK PIONEER STAGING AREA on the Pulaski Drive side. ACCESSIBILITY: the Dry Creek Garden lot at the end of May Road is the disabled-accessible parking for this park, and it is the lot attached to the attraction that is currently closed. The rest of the accessibility text on this page describes Garin's facilities -- the Garin Barn restrooms, the Jordan Pond chemical toilet, the picnic-area fountains -- which is what two parks sharing one page's boilerplate looks like. CATTLE ARE GRAZED HERE, same warning as Garin: heel or leash dogs past cattle, because chasing may injure or kill them.
